locators: Page 1, Indications for use
text: US labeling indicates Neuroform Atlas with neurovascular embolic coils for patients age 18 or older with wide-neck intracranial saccular aneurysms arising from a 2.0-4.5 mm parent vessel that are not amenable to surgical clipping; wide neck is defined as neck at least 4 mm or dome-to-neck ratio below 2.

locators: Page 1, Contraindications
text: US labeling contraindicates Neuroform Atlas in patients for whom antiplatelet and/or anticoagulation therapy is contraindicated.

locators: Page 1, Warnings, fifth bullet
text: Select stent length to maintain at least 4 mm beyond each side of the aneurysm neck along the parent vessel; the labeling states that the stent is not designed for an aneurysm neck longer than 22 mm.

locators: Page 1, Cautions / precautions, fifth bullet
text: The labeling states that Neuroform Atlas may foreshorten by up to 6.3% after deployment.

locators: Page 1, Cautions / precautions, sixth and seventh bullets
text: The coiling microcatheter maximum outer diameter should not exceed that of the stent-delivery microcatheter; standard interventional devices with distal tips greater than 1.8 F may not pass through the stent interstices.

locators: Page 1, Magnetic Resonance Imaging Safety Information
text: The implant is MR Conditional immediately after placement at 1.5 or 3.0 T, with maximum spatial gradient 2500 G/cm, whole-body averaged SAR 2 W/kg, and head-averaged SAR 3.2 W/kg; the stated maximum temperature rise applies after 15 minutes of continuous scanning under those conditions.

locators: PDF page 1, HDE statement beneath the title
text: The River Stent System is a Humanitarian Device authorized by Federal law for use in the treatment of idiopathic intracranial hypertension in adult patients who have failed medical therapy; the labeling states that the effectiveness of the device for this use has not been demonstrated.

locators: PDF page 4, section 3 Indications for Use
text: US labeling indicates the River Stent System for stenting of the venous sinus in adults (22 years or older) with idiopathic intracranial hypertension who have failed medical therapy, have a significant venous sinus stenosis (>50% stenosis and pressure gradient >=8 mmHg), and have an upstream venous sinus diameter between 5 mm and 8.5 mm; patients must also meet at least one of two further criteria: (1) intractable headache (HIT-6 score >59) with papilledema or a history of papilledema and at least 6 months of failed medical therapy, with obese patients (BMI >=30) also having completed at least 6 months of a weight-management program without adequate relief, or (2) moderate to severe papilledema (Frisen grade >=2), transient visual obscuration, or sixth nerve palsy after failed medical therapy with the treating ophthalmologist judging vision to be at risk.

locators: PDF page 4, section 4 Contraindications (first two bullets)
PDF page 5, section 4 Contraindications (remaining bullets)
text: US labeling contraindicates the River Stent System in patients in whom anticoagulant, antiplatelet, or thrombolytic drugs are contraindicated; patients with a thrombophilic disorder or anticardiolipin syndrome; known hypersensitivity to nitinol or its components (nickel, titanium); known allergy to contrast or anesthetic drug despite premedication; anatomy that does not permit passage or deployment of the stent; active bacterial infection; a pre-existing stent at the target transverse-sigmoid sinus; and renal insufficiency not on dialysis.

locators: PDF page 19, Table 17 Stent Sizes
text: The River Stent is supplied in three sizes, all 70 mm long and tapered: SRS70-0910 (proximal 10.5 mm, distal 9.0 mm, distal perimeter 25 mm), SRS70-0708 (proximal 8.0 mm, distal 7.0 mm, distal perimeter 20 mm), and SRS70-0608 (proximal 8.0 mm, distal 6.0 mm, distal perimeter 17 mm).

locators: PDF page 19, section 10.2 Stent Size Selection
text: Size selection per labeling: measure the perimeter of the transverse sinus at its upstream third (the landing zone of the distal end of the stent) on pre-treatment MR venography, CT venography, or 3D catheter venography, and select the stent whose distal perimeter is immediately larger than the measured sinus perimeter (Table 17); appropriate size selection is required for wall apposition.

locators: PDF page 18, section 10.1 Required Materials
text: Labeling lists the required adjunctive materials: an introducer sheath of minimum 6F with minimum inner diameter 0.078 in (2 mm); a guide catheter of minimum 6F with minimum inner diameter 0.070 in (1.778 mm); an exchange-length (>300 cm) 0.014 in (0.36 mm) guidewire with a J-shaped tip; a microcatheter with minimum inner diameter 0.017 in; and a 5-10 cc saline flushing syringe.

locators: PDF page 5, section 5 Warnings, bullets on resistance and repositioning
text: Labeling warns not to reposition the River Stent in the transverse-sigmoid sinus: once deployment has started the stent must be entirely deployed; if unusual resistance is felt during access, the stent and delivery catheter are to be removed as a single unit.

locators: PDF page 6, section 6 Precautions
text: Labeling states that appropriate antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy should be administered before insertion of the River Stent System, and recommends a soft-tip J-shaped guidewire to avoid involuntary catheterization of a cortical vein during sinus catheterization and over-the-wire exchange.

locators: PDF page 6-7, section 7 Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) Safety Information
text: The River Stent is MR Conditional: 1.5 T or 3.0 T static field, maximum spatial field gradient 40 T/m (4,000 gauss/cm), circularly polarized RF excitation with no transmit-coil restriction, Normal Operating Mode, whole-body averaged SAR 2 W/kg for 60 minutes of continuous RF exposure; the implant produces an imaging artifact and may create susceptibility artifacts on MR venography that degrade assessment of lumen patency.

locators: PDF page 5 (English section), Indications for Use
text: US labeling indicates the Zilver Vascular Stent as an adjunct to percutaneous transluminal angioplasty in the treatment of symptomatic vascular disease of the iliac arteries up to 100 mm in length with a reference vessel diameter of 5 to 9 mm, in patients who are suitable candidates for PTA and/or stent treatment. The labeling does not address venous sinus or intracranial use.

locators: PDF page 5 (English section), Contraindications and Warnings
text: The labeling states there are no contraindications known at this time based on the clinical data; it warns that persons allergic to nitinol (nickel titanium) may suffer an allergic reaction to the implant.

locators: PDF page 5 (English section), Device Description size matrix
text: The Zilver Vascular Stent is available in outer diameters of 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 mm and lengths of 20, 30, 40, 60, and 80 mm, each preloaded on 5 French (1.67 mm), 6 French (2.0 mm), or 7 French (2.3 mm) delivery systems; hand-loading is not possible.

locators: PDF page 15 (English section), Table 10 Stent Size Selection Table
text: Table 10 size selection: reference vessel diameter 5.0 mm -> 6.0 mm nominal stent; 5.0-6.0 mm -> 7.0 mm; 6.0-7.0 mm -> 8.0 mm; 7.0-8.0 mm -> 9.0 mm; 8.0-9.0 mm -> 10.0 mm.

locators: PDF page 15 (English section), Directions for Use step 2 and step 4
text: The 7.0 and 6.0 French (2.3 and 2.0 mm) delivery systems accept a 0.035 inch (0.89 mm) wire guide; the 5.0 French (1.67 mm) system accepts a 0.018 inch (0.46 mm) wire guide; an extra- or ultra-stiff wire guide is specified and predilatation is recommended.

locators: PDF page 7 (English section), MR Conditional
text: The Zilver Vascular Stent is MR Conditional per non-clinical testing: static field 3 Tesla or less, spatial gradient 720 gauss/cm or less, whole-body averaged SAR 1.5 W/kg for 20 minutes (single stent at 1.5 T) and 3 W/kg for 15 minutes (single stent at 3 T, or overlapping stents at 1.5 and 3 T); maximum temperature rises of 0.1-3.8 degrees C were observed under those conditions.

attributes.indicated_use: Indicated for use to restore blood flow in the neurovasculature by removing thrombus for the treatment of acute ischemic stroke to reduce disability in patients with a persistent, proximal anterior circulation, large vessel occlusion, and smaller core infarcts who have first received IV tPA; endovascular therapy with the device should be started within 6 hours of symptom onset; indicated to restore blood flow by removing thrombus from a large intracranial vessel in patients experiencing ischemic stroke within 8 hours of symptom onset; patients who are ineligible for IV tPA or who fail IV tPA therapy are candidates for treatment

attributes.indicated_use: Indicated for use to restore blood flow in the neurovasculature by removing thrombus for the treatment of acute ischemic stroke to reduce disability in patients with a persistent, proximal anterior circulation, large vessel occlusion, and smaller core infarcts who have first received intravenous tissue plasminogen activator (IV t-PA); endovascular therapy with the device should start within 6 hours of symptom onset; intended to restore blood flow in the neurovasculature by removing thrombus in patients experiencing ischemic stroke within 8 hours of symptom onset; patients who are ineligible for intravenous tissue plasminogen activator (IV t-PA) or who fail IV t-PA therapy are candidates for treatment; indicated for use to restore blood flow in the neurovasculature by removing thrombus for the treatment of acute ischemic stroke to reduce disability in patients with a persistent, proximal anterior circulation, large-vessel occlusion of the internal carotid artery (ICA) or middle cerebral artery (MCA)-M1 segments with smaller-core infarcts (0– 50 mL for age < 80 years, 0–20 mL for age ≥ 80 years); endovascular therapy with the device should start within 6–24 hours of time last seen well in patients who are ineligible for intravenous tissue plasminogen activator (IV t- PA) or who fail IV t-PA therapy

locators: wedge-1.png, Indications for Use
text: The Wedge Microcatheter is intended for general intravascular use, including the peripheral, coronary and neuro vasculature, for the infusion of diagnostic agents such as contrast media and therapeutic agents.

locators: wedge-1.png, Contraindications
text: The Wedge Microcatheter IFU states there are no known contraindications.

locators: wedge-2.png, compatibility table under Preparation for Use
text: Wedge Microcatheter 21: shaft length 160 cm; guide / aspiration catheter minimum ID 0.070 in (1.78 mm); guidewire recommendation <= 0.018 in (<= 0.46 mm).

locators: wedge-3.png, dimensions table under Directions for Use
text: Wedge Microcatheter 21: inner diameter 0.53 mm (0.0210 in); dead space (average) 0.54 cc; maximum distal OD 1.73 mm (0.068 in).

locators: wedge-2.png Warnings; wedge-3.png flow-rate table
text: Infusion pressure should not exceed 300 psi to avoid potential rupture of the Wedge Microcatheter; approximate nominal flow rates for Wedge 21 are 0.77 cc/s (saline, 100 psi), 1.90 cc/s (saline, 300 psi), 0.52 / 1.16 cc/s (60% contrast, 100 / 300 psi), and 0.20 / 0.73 cc/s (76% contrast, 100 / 300 psi).

locators: wedge-2.png, Steam Shaping
text: Tip steam shaping per IFU: over-bend the shaping mandrel by about one-third (a 60 degree mandrel bend for a 45 degree tip), hold the tip/mandrel assembly approximately one inch from a steam source for approximately 30 seconds, then set in heparinized saline; the shaping mandrel is not for use inside the body.

review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: When vasospasm stops blood flow.
text: The IFU states use of the Onyx LES is contraindicated when optimal catheter placement is not possible, when prevascular testing indicates intolerance to the occlusion procedure, or when vasospasm stops blood flow.

PDF page 8, DIRECTIONS FOR USE step 3
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: Use only ev3 approved, Onyx™ LES/DMSO compatible micro catheters indicated for use in the neurovasculature
text: The IFU requires use of only ev3-approved, Onyx LES/DMSO compatible microcatheters indicated for the neurovasculature, together with ev3 syringes; other microcatheters or syringes may not be compatible with DMSO and their use can result in thromboembolic events due to catheter degradation. No specific competitor or third-party microcatheter is named as compatible.

PDF page 8, HOW SUPPLIED
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: Onyx™ LES 18 (6% EVOH) and Onyx™ LES 34 (8% EVOH)
text: US labeling describes two Onyx LES formulations: Onyx LES 18 (6% EVOH copolymer, nominal viscosity 18 cSt at 40 degrees C), recommended when feeding-pedicle embolization will be conducted close to the nidus, and Onyx LES 34 (8% EVOH copolymer, nominal viscosity 33 cSt at 40 degrees C), recommended for embolizing higher-flow and larger fistulous components; Onyx LES 18 travels more distally and penetrates deeper into the nidus than Onyx LES 34 due to its lower viscosity.

locators: PDF page 8, DIRECTIONS FOR USE step 1
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: Shake the Onyx™ LES at least 20 minutes on an Onyx™ LES mixer at a setting of 5
text: The IFU instructs shaking the Onyx LES for at least 20 minutes on an Onyx LES mixer at a setting of 5, continuing mixing until ready to inject; failure to continuously mix for the required time may result in inadequate suspension of the tantalum and inadequate fluoroscopic visualization during delivery.

locators: PDF page 8, DIRECTIONS FOR USE steps 4-5
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: aspirate approximately 0.8 ml of ev3 DMSO into the yellow ev3 1 ml DMSO syringe
text: The IFU directs flushing contrast from the microcatheter with 10 ml of saline, then aspirating approximately 0.8 ml of ev3 DMSO into the yellow ev3 1 ml DMSO syringe and injecting DMSO into the delivery microcatheter in sufficient volume to fill the catheter deadspace, referring to the delivery catheter labeling for exact deadspace volume; only the ev3 1 ml syringe is to be used to inject DMSO and the Onyx LES.

PDF page 8, DIRECTIONS FOR USE step 7
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: recommended that the Onyx™ LES be injected at a slow, steady rate of 0.16 ml/min
text: The IFU recommends injecting the Onyx LES at a slow, steady rate of 0.16 mL/min (0.25 ml/90 sec) using only thumb pressure, and states the injection rate must not exceed 0.3 ml/min.

review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: Do not allow more than 1 cm of the Onyx™ LES to reflux back over catheter tip
text: The IFU warns not to allow more than 1 cm of the Onyx LES to reflux back over the catheter tip, and that angioarchitecture, vasospasm, excessive Onyx LES reflux, or prolonged injection time may result in difficult catheter removal and potential entrapment.

locators: PDF page 3, WARNINGS
PDF page 9, WARNINGS
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: DO NOT interrupt the Onyx™ LES injection for longer than two minutes prior to re-injection
text: The IFU states that the Onyx LES injection must not be interrupted for longer than two minutes prior to re-injection, because solidification of the Onyx LES may occur at the catheter tip resulting in catheter occlusion, and use of excessive pressure to clear the catheter may result in catheter rupture.

locators: PDF page 3, WARNINGS
PDF page 8, DIRECTIONS FOR USE step 7
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: rapid injection of DMSO into the vasculature may lead to vasospasm and/or angionecrosis
text: The IFU warns that animal studies have shown rapid injection of DMSO into the vasculature may lead to vasospasm and/or angionecrosis, and that using the palm of the hand rather than thumb pressure to advance the plunger may result in overpressurization in the event of catheter occlusion.

review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: A garlic-like taste may be noted by the patient with use of the Onyx™ LES
text: The IFU notes as a precaution that a garlic-like taste may be noted by the patient with use of the Onyx LES due to the DMSO component, may last several hours, and an odor on the breath and skin may be present.

locators: PDF page 3, WARNINGS
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (onyx-les.json).
source_quote: use of monopolar electrocautery devices for surgical resection of bAVMs ... should be avoided
text: The IFU warns that due to the possibility of electrical arcing with the tantalum metal in the Onyx LES material, use of monopolar electrocautery devices for surgical resection of bAVMs or arteriovenous fistulas embolized with the Onyx LES should be avoided, and bipolar devices should be used with caution.

source_quote: do not attempt to clear or inject any material through it
text: The IFU warns that after using a microcatheter with the Onyx LES, one should not attempt to clear or inject any material through it, as such attempts may lead to embolus or embolization of an unintended area.

source_quote: Excessive force to remove an entrapped catheter may cause serious intracranial hemorrhage
text: The IFU warns that excessive force to remove an entrapped catheter may cause serious intracranial hemorrhage, and that the long-term effects of an entrapped catheter left in a patient are unknown but potentially could include clot formation, infection, or catheter migration; difficult removal/entrapment may be caused by angioarchitecture, vasospasm, reflux, or injection time.

text: The IFU warns to stop injection if the Onyx LES is not visualized exiting the catheter tip, because testing has shown that over-pressurization and catheter rupture can occur if only a volume of 0.05 ml of the Onyx LES is injected without being visualized exiting the catheter tip.

text: US labeling indicates the WEB Aneurysm Embolization System for endovascular treatment of adult patients with saccular, wide neck bifurcation intracranial aneurysms at the middle cerebral artery (MCA) bifurcation, internal carotid artery (ICA) terminus, anterior communicating artery (AComm) complex, or basilar artery apex, with dome diameter from 3 mm to 10 mm and either neck size 4 mm or greater, or a dome-to-neck ratio greater than 1 and less than 2.

text: The IFU instructs measuring the aneurysm neck, average diameter, and height in two orthogonal 2D-angiographic projections, then choosing the WEB device using the average width and smallest height measurements: the correct WEB size is approximately 1 mm larger than the average aneurysm diameter and approximately 1 mm smaller than the smallest aneurysm height.

text: US labeling directs WEB shape selection by the average aneurysm diameter-to-average aneurysm neck ratio: the WEB SL shape fits aneurysms with a 1-to-1 through 1.5-to-1 ratio, and the WEB SLS shape fits aneurysms with a 1.5-to-1 to 2-to-1 ratio.

review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (web.json).
source_quote: should not be retracted and deployed more than twice
text: The IFU states the WEB embolization device should not be retracted and deployed more than twice; after two attempts, the device must be removed and replaced with another WEB device of the same or alternate size, because thrombus can prevent full deployment and recapture and residence beyond the activated clotting time (ACT) is not permitted for an inappropriately sized or non-optimally positioned device.

text: US labeling warns the WEB embolization device cannot be detached with any power source other than a WEB detachment control device, and instructs that at least two WEB detachment control devices be available before initiating an embolization procedure.

text: The IFU notes the WEB embolization device foreshortens approximately 60% during delivery; for example, an 11 mm x 9 mm device measures approximately 20 mm in length when contained within a 0.032-0.038 inch delivery microcatheter.

text: US labeling requires the WEB embolization device be delivered only through a compatible microcatheter with a PTFE inner surface coating; use of an incompatible microcatheter may damage the device and delivery system and necessitate removal of both from the patient.

text: US labeling states the WEB Aneurysm Embolization Device is MR Conditional: it can be scanned safely at a static magnetic field of 3 Tesla or less, maximum spatial gradient field of 4,000 Gauss/cm (40 T/m), and maximum whole-body-averaged SAR of 2.0 W/kg for 15 minutes of scanning (per pulse sequence) in Normal Operating Mode, producing an expected maximum temperature rise of +1.4°C after 15 minutes of continuous scanning; image artifact extends approximately 5 mm from the implant on a 3-Tesla gradient echo sequence.

text: US labeling indicates the FRED System for use in the internal carotid artery from the petrous segment to the terminus for endovascular treatment of adult patients (22 years of age or older) with wide-necked (neck width ≥ 4 mm or dome-to-neck ratio < 2) saccular or fusiform intracranial aneurysms arising from a parent vessel with a diameter ≥ 2.0 mm and ≤ 5.0 mm.

locators: PDF page 2, Contraindications
review_note: Drafted from the retained IFU by an independent agent with page locators and a verbatim anchor quote (fred.json).
source_quote: Patients who have not received dual anti-platelet agents prior to the procedure
text: The IFU contraindicates the FRED System in patients in whom anticoagulant, anti-platelet therapy, or thrombolytic drugs are contraindicated; patients with known hypersensitivity to metal such as nickel-titanium; patients with anatomy that does not permit passage or deployment of the device; patients with an active bacterial infection; patients with a pre-existing stent in place at the target aneurysm; patients in whom the parent vessel size does not fall within the indicated range; and patients who have not received dual anti-platelet agents prior to the procedure.

text: US labeling warns that a slight decrease in the proportion of patients achieving complete aneurysm occlusion without significant parent artery stenosis was observed with device use in the communicating segment (C7) of the ICA (52.6%, 10/19 subjects in the FRED IDE study at 1 year), and recommends weighing benefits and risks of alternative treatments before treating C7 aneurysms with retrograde-filling risk factors such as a fetal-origin posterior communicating artery.

text: The IFU warns that placement of multiple FRED implants may increase the risk of ischemic complications, and that delayed rupture may occur with large and giant intracranial aneurysms.
